s565: A structurally separated element of the road that divides adjacent carriageways and is not intended for trackless vehicles to drive on
s566: Any of the longitudinal strips into which the carriageway may be divided, whether or not it is marked with longitudinal road markings
s567: The part of the road normally used by trackless vehicles
s569: According to paragraph 9 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a dividing strip is a structurally separated element of the road that divides adjacent carriageways and is not intended for trackless vehicles to drive on.
s570: Passing one or more vehicles moving ahead in the same direction in the same lane, by leaving the lane you are in
s571: Passing one or more vehicles coming from the opposite direction in the neighbouring lane
s572: A vehicle moving faster in lanes for the same direction than vehicles in the lanes nearer the edge of the carriageway
s574: According to paragraph 10 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, overtaking is passing one or more vehicles moving ahead in the same direction in the same lane, by leaving the lane you are in.
s575: A place where roads cross, join or branch on the same level, including the areas formed by such crossing, joining or branching
s576: A place where exits from adjacent territory cross roads
s577: A crossing of carriageways at different levels
s579: According to paragraph 13 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, an intersection is a place where roads cross, join or branch on the same level, including the areas formed by such crossing, joining or branching. A place where exits from adjacent territory cross roads is not considered an intersection.
s580: An area with buildings whose entrances and exits are marked with the appropriate road signs
s581: Any road intended for heavy pedestrian traffic
s584: According to paragraph 17 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a built-up area is an area with buildings whose entrances and exits are marked with the appropriate road signs.
s585: The period from dusk to dawn
s586: The period from dawn to dusk
s589: According to paragraph 21 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the dark time of day is the period from dusk to dawn.
s590: A road or part of a road intended for cycling, marked with the appropriate road sign and structurally separated from other roads or from other elements of the road
s591: A lane of the carriageway intended for cycling. A cycle lane is separated from the rest of the carriageway by longitudinal road markings
s593: According to paragraph 23 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a bicycle path (cycle path) is a road or part of a road intended for cycling, marked with the appropriate road sign and structurally separated from other roads or from other elements of the road.
s594: The maximum speed of a vehicle as set by its manufacturer
s595: The speed shown on the "Speed limit" identification sign fixed to the vehicle
s596: The maximum speed limit set for the vehicle on the given section of road
s598: According to paragraph 29 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, design speed is the maximum speed of a vehicle as set by its manufacturer.
s599: An area directly next to the road that is not intended for through traffic (a yard, a housing estate, a car park, a petrol station, a business, etc.)
s600: An element of the road intended for trackless vehicles (other than the sidewalk, the shoulder, the cycle path and the footpath)
s602: According to paragraph 38 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, adjacent territory is an area directly next to the road that is not intended for through traffic (a yard, a housing estate, a car park, a petrol station, a business, etc.)
s603: Any of the longitudinal strips into which the carriageway may be divided, whether or not it is marked with longitudinal road markings, that is wide enough for one line of motor vehicles other than motorcycles
s604: The whole surface of a road or street open to traffic
s605: A structurally separated element of the road that divides adjacent carriageways
s607: According to paragraph 45 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "lane" is any of the longitudinal strips into which the carriageway may be divided, whether or not it is marked with longitudinal road markings, that is wide enough for one line of motor vehicles other than motorcycles.
s608: A motorised vehicle whose design speed does not exceed 40 km/h, or which cannot exceed that speed, or is prohibited from exceeding it for a reason not related to traffic flow
s609: A motorised or non-motorised vehicle whose design speed does not exceed 45 km/h
s610: Any vehicle that travels on the road at no more than 50 km/h
s612: According to paragraph 53 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "slow-moving vehicle" is a motorised vehicle whose design speed does not exceed 40 km/h, or which cannot exceed that speed, or is prohibited from exceeding it for a reason not related to traffic flow.
s613: A crossing, on the same level, of a road and railway or tram tracks that have their own track bed
s614: A crossing, at different levels, of a road and railway or tram tracks that have their own track bed
s617: According to paragraph 58 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "railway crossing" is a crossing, on the same level, of a road and railway or tram tracks that have their own track bed.
s618: A vehicle intended to carry passengers on the road, travelling on a set route
s619: Any bus with more than 16 seats, not counting the driver's seat
s620: Any vehicle that is intended for carrying goods or for transporting people
s622: According to paragraph 67 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "route vehicle" is a vehicle intended to carry passengers on the road, travelling on a set route.
s623: An area with buildings where special traffic rules apply and whose entrances and exits are marked with the appropriate road signs
s625: According to paragraph 75 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "residential zone" is an area with buildings where special traffic rules apply and whose entrances and exits are marked with the appropriate road signs.
s626: An element of the road that adjoins the carriageway or is separated from it structurally or by a lawn, and is intended for pedestrians
s627: A path intended for pedestrians, separated from the road
s630: According to paragraph 83 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "sidewalk" is an element of the road that adjoins the carriageway or is separated from it structurally or by a lawn, and is intended for pedestrians.
s631: A path intended for pedestrians, separated from the road. A footpath may be marked with the appropriate road sign
s632: An element of the road that adjoins the carriageway and is intended for pedestrians
s633: Any section of road intended for pedestrians
s635: According to paragraph 85 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "footpath" is a path intended for pedestrians, separated from the road. A footpath may be marked with the appropriate road sign.
s636: A situation in which a sharp bend, the crest of a hill, trees and plants, a roadside structure or an obstacle on the road reduces visibility in the direction of travel so much that driving at the maximum permitted speed on that section of road may be dangerous
s637: A reduction of road visibility to less than 300 metres in a tunnel, during the dark time of day, or in fog, rain, snow or other natural conditions
s639: According to paragraph 89 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, "limited visibility" is a situation in which a sharp bend, the crest of a hill, trees and plants, a roadside structure or an obstacle on the road reduces visibility in the direction of travel so much that driving at the maximum permitted speed on that section of road may be dangerous.
s640: A person who is in or on a vehicle, or is getting into or out of it, but is not driving it
s641: A person who uses roller skates to get around
s642: A person who is actually driving the vehicle
s644: According to paragraph 34 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "passenger" is a person who is in or on a vehicle, or is getting into or out of it, but is not driving it.
s645: A motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle or moped) with a maximum permitted mass of no more than 3500 kg and no more than 8 seats, not counting the driver's seat
s646: A motorcycle with a gross mass of up to 2500 kg
s647: A motor vehicle with a gross mass of up to 4500 kg and more than 8 but no more than 12 seats, not counting the driver's seat
s649: According to paragraph 46 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "passenger car" is a motor vehicle (other than a motorcycle) with a maximum permitted mass of up to 3500 kg and no more than 8 seats, not counting the driver's seat.
s650: A trailer with a maximum permitted mass of no more than 750 kg
s651: A trailer with an unladen weight of no more than 850 kg
s652: A trailer with a gross mass of no more than 950 kg
s654: According to paragraph 48 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "light trailer" is a trailer with a maximum permitted mass of no more than 750 kg.
s655: A device moving on the road, or intended to move on it, that is propelled by an engine or another force
s656: Only a motorised device moving on the road, or intended to move on it, that is normally used on the road to carry people or goods
s658: According to paragraph 73 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a "vehicle" is a device moving on the road, or intended to move on the road, that is propelled by an engine or another force.
s662: What is meant by the driver's reaction time?
s659: The time from noticing a danger to taking the measures needed to avoid it
s660: The time from noticing a danger until the vehicle comes to a complete stop
s661: The time needed to move your foot from the accelerator pedal to the brake pedal
s663: The driver's reaction time means the time from noticing a danger to taking the measures needed to avoid it.
s668: The relevant bodies of the executive authorities and local self-government, within their powers, restrict or temporarily stop traffic on a road:
s664: In any of the circumstances listed
s665: Only in the event of an accident, a disaster or another kind of calamity
s666: Only to ensure road safety and to protect human life, health and property
s667: Only when the road is in poor condition, when visibility is limited, during natural phenomena and during natural disasters
s669: According to subparagraph "a" of paragraph 1 of Article 13 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, traffic on a road is restricted or temporarily stopped when the road is in poor condition, when visibility is limited, during natural phenomena, or in the event of a natural disaster, an accident, a disaster or another calamity, to ensure road safety and to protect human life, health and property. This is done by the relevant bodies of the executive authorities of Georgia and of local self-government, within their powers.
s672: Is it allowed to change the way traffic is organised, in order to increase road capacity or for another purpose, at the expense of road safety?
s673: According to paragraph 2 of Article 14 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, changing the way traffic is organised, in order to increase road capacity or for another purpose, at the expense of road safety is not allowed.
s678: Which of the following activities is prohibited without a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agency), or without agreement with that body (agency)?
s674: Any of the activities listed in this question
s675: Only carrying passengers by taxi in a passenger car (category M1) in the capital of Georgia
s676: Only holding mass, sports and other events on the road
s677: Only regular passenger transport on set routes (including regular passenger transport within the administrative boundaries of a municipality)
s679: According to subparagraphs "c", "d" and "e" of paragraph 1 of Article 17 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, to ensure road safety, the following activities are allowed only after obtaining a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agencies), or in agreement with that body (agency), in the manner set by the legislation of Georgia: c) placing a kiosk or another object right next to the road that may reduce visibility and/or hinder drivers and pedestrians; d) regular passenger transport on set routes (including local regular urban passenger transport); e) holding mass, sports and other events on the road.
s684: Which of the following activities is prohibited without a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agency), or without agreement with that body (agency)?
s680: Any of the actions listed in this question
s681: Only fitting special light and sound signals, and also a special loudspeaker
s682: Only driving a vehicle that carries dangerous goods
s685: According to subparagraph "f" of paragraph 1 of Article 17 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, to ensure road safety, the following activities are allowed only after obtaining a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agency), or in agreement with that body (agency), in the manner set by the legislation of Georgia: f) modifying a vehicle, fitting it with special flashing lights and/or sound signals and/or a special loudspeaker, and/or giving a vehicle a special colour scheme, and/or painting slanted white stripes on the sides of the vehicle's body.
s690: A road user has the right to receive, in the manner set by the legislation of Georgia, from the competent state and local self-government bodies and from other authorised persons, information:
s686: Any of the information listed in this question
s687: Only about the reasons for restricting or stopping traffic on the road
s688: Only about the quality of products and services related to ensuring road safety
s689: Only about the safety conditions for traffic on the road
s691: According to subparagraphs "b.a", "b.b" and "b.c" of paragraph 1 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road user has the right to receive, in the manner set by the legislation of Georgia, from the competent state and local self-government bodies and from other authorised persons: b.a) information about the safety conditions for traffic on the road; b.b) information about the reasons for restricting or stopping traffic on the road; b.c) information about the quality of products and services related to ensuring road safety.
s694: Does a road user have the right to restrict traffic and/or create a danger by stacking, dumping or leaving objects on the road, or by creating any other obstacle on it?
s695: According to paragraph 3 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road user must not restrict traffic and/or create a danger by stacking, dumping or leaving objects on the road, or by creating any other obstacle on it.
s698: If a road user has restricted traffic and/or created a danger by dumping objects on the road or by creating any other obstacle on it, they must immediately:
s696: Take the measures needed to remove it, and if this cannot be done immediately, make sure that other road users are warned about it in good time
s697: Report it to the cleaning service of the relevant local self-government body and continue driving with particular care
s699: According to paragraph 3 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road user must not restrict traffic and/or create a danger by stacking, dumping or leaving objects on the road, or by creating any other obstacle on it. A road user who, for an objective reason, could not avoid creating such a restriction or danger must immediately take the measures needed to remove it, and if this cannot be done immediately, must make sure that other road users are warned about it in good time.
s702: If a road user has restricted traffic and/or created a danger by stacking or dumping objects on the road and, for an objective reason, cannot immediately take the measures needed to remove the restriction or danger, they must:
s700: Make sure that other road users are warned about it in good time
s701: Continue driving with particular care; they are not required to warn other road users about the restriction or danger
s707: When using the interior rear-view mirror of a passenger car, the driver must bear in mind:
s703: All of the points listed in this question
s704: Only that objects in a convex mirror appear further away than they really are
s705: Only that the mirror has "blind spots", so it cannot always give a full field of view or let you keep track of an overtaking vehicle
s706: Only that the mirror must be adjusted to suit the driver's height
s708: When using the interior rear-view mirror of a passenger car, the driver must bear in mind that the mirror must be adjusted to suit the driver's height, that objects in a convex mirror appear further away than they really are, and that the mirror has "blind spots", so it cannot always give a full field of view or let you keep track of an overtaking vehicle.
s710: May road users exercise their rights if this would restrict or violate the rights of other road users?
s711: According to paragraph 2 of Article 20 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road user exercising their rights must not restrict or violate the rights of other road users. A road user must not, by their actions, create a danger or an obstacle to traffic. They must not endanger people or cause damage to state, public or private property.
s715: If a driver notices another driver on the road who is aggressive and behaving provocatively, they:
s712: Must stay calm and keep control of their vehicle
s713: Must urge the aggressive driver to calm down by giving two long and one short blast of the horn
s716: According to subparagraph "k" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on the road the driver must bear in mind the following: if the driver notices another driver on the road who is aggressive and behaving provocatively, they must stay calm and keep control of their vehicle.
s720: A driver must drive a vehicle:
s717: Calmly, without showing aggression and without trying to show off as superior on the road
s718: Calmly, but trying to show that they are superior on the road
s719: Aggressively, as someone superior on the road
s721: According to subparagraph "n" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when driving on the road the driver must bear in mind the following: the driver must drive the vehicle calmly, without showing aggression and without trying to show off as superior on the road.
s726: Apart from the carriageway, which of the following elements may a road include?
s722: The tram tracks, as well as the sidewalk, the shoulder, the dividing strip and the cycle path
s724: Only the tram tracks and the sidewalk
s725: Only the shoulder and the dividing strip
s727: According to paragraph 12 of Article 5 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a road is the whole surface of a road or street open to traffic. A road may have one carriageway or several carriageways clearly separated by a dividing strip, or carriageways at different levels. This term may include the tram tracks, the sidewalk, the shoulder, the dividing strip and the cycle path.
s731: The plate confirming that a motor vehicle has passed its roadworthiness test is issued by:
s729: The Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia
s732: According to paragraph 6 of Article 11 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the plate confirming that a motor vehicle has passed its roadworthiness test is issued by the testing centre.
s736: If a driver is approaching a traffic light that has been showing a light allowing movement for a long time, they must:
s733: Continue driving so that they are ready to stop the vehicle safely at any moment
s734: Speed up, even beyond the speed limit, to get through that section of road before the traffic light switches to a light prohibiting movement
s735: Speed up and watch the traffic light signals
s737: If a driver is approaching a traffic light that has been showing a light allowing movement for a long time, they must continue driving so that they are ready to stop the vehicle safely at any moment.
s741: What does a seat belt do in a road traffic accident?
s738: It does everything listed in this question
s739: It only holds the driver and passengers in a position that allows the airbags to open safely
s740: It only stops the driver and passengers from being thrown forward by inertia, and so from hitting parts of the vehicle's interior and other passengers
s742: In a road traffic accident, a seat belt both stops the driver and passengers from being thrown forward by inertia, and so from hitting parts of the vehicle's interior and other passengers, and holds the driver and passengers in a position that allows the airbags to open safely.
s745: Without a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agency), or without agreement with that body (agency), it is not allowed to drive:
s743: Both an oversized (large) or overweight (heavy) vehicle on the road and a vehicle carrying dangerous goods
s744: Only an oversized (large) or overweight (heavy) vehicle on the road
s746: According to subparagraphs "g" and "h" of paragraph 1 of Article 17 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, to ensure road safety, the following activities are allowed only after obtaining a permit, authorisation or consent from the relevant competent body (agency), or in agreement with that body (agency), in the manner set by the legislation of Georgia: g) driving an oversized (large) or overweight (heavy) vehicle on the road; h) driving a vehicle carrying dangerous goods.
s751: Apart from the authorised officers of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia, traffic may also be directed, within the powers granted to them by law, by:
s747: Any of the persons listed in this question
s750: Only rescuers and people taking part in rescue work
s752: According to subparagraphs "c", "f" and "g" of paragraph 3 of Article 30 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, traffic is directed by the authorised officers of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia. Within the powers granted to them by the legislation of Georgia, traffic may also be directed by: c) rescuers and people taking part in rescue work, to make sure the rescue work can be carried out; f) railway employees, at a railway crossing; g) ferry transport operators, in a port.
s756: What must happen if a cable or pipe is found in the ground during work?
s753: Work must stop immediately and may continue only after official permission is received
s757: If a cable or pipe is found in the ground during work, work must stop immediately and may continue after official permission is received.
s761: When putting the machine into working mode or before moving it, to make sure no outsiders are in the work area, the operator:
s759: Must give a warning signal by hand
s760: Must get down to the work area and warn outsiders personally
s762: When putting the machine into working mode or before moving it, to make sure no outsiders are in the work area, the operator must sound the horn.
s766: Before work starts, a sign must be put up at the work site with information:
s765: The operator's surname, first name and patronymic
s767: Before work starts, a sign must be put up at the work site with information about the work in progress.
s771: May outsiders be allowed onto an excavator?
s772: Outsiders may not be allowed onto an excavator.
s776: When getting off an excavator, you must:
s773: Do everything listed in this question
s774: Only put all the controls in the neutral position
s775: Only switch off all the controls
s777: When getting off an excavator, you must switch off all the controls and put them in the neutral position.
s781: May a machine be left running?
s782: A machine may not be left running.
s786: May a loaded excavator bucket be left raised off the ground?
s783: No, the bucket must be lowered to the ground
s784: Yes, at a height of 1-1.5 metres above the ground
s787: If an excavator bucket is left loaded, it must be lowered to the ground.
s792: Which mechanism is used in internal combustion engines?
s793: Internal combustion engines use a valve train (gas distribution mechanism).
s797: Which drive is used between rotating shafts whose axes are not aligned and meet at a changing angle?
s798: A cardan (universal joint) drive is used between rotating shafts whose axes are not aligned and meet at a changing angle.
s803: Which power source supplies all electrical consumers when the engine is running at low speed?
s804: When the engine is running at low speed, all electrical consumers are supplied by the battery.
s805: Which power source supplies all electrical consumers when the engine is running at medium and high speed?
s806: When the engine is running at medium and high speed, all electrical consumers are supplied by the alternator (generator).
s810: Where may luggage be carried on a motorcycle?
s807: In the motorcycle's luggage bag or on its luggage rack
s809: On the right and left of the handlebars, evenly distributed
s811: On a motorcycle, luggage may be carried in the motorcycle's luggage bag or on its luggage rack.
s814: When putting a motorcycle on its centre stand, you must pay attention to the following:
s812: The surface under the centre stand must be firm
s813: The motorcycle may be put on the centre stand only for a short time
s815: When putting a motorcycle on its centre stand, you must make sure that the surface under the centre stand is firm.
s820: When is there a risk of a motorcycle being pushed sideways at high speed?
s816: In any of the circumstances listed in this question
s818: Only if the two front brake discs act differently from each other when braking
s819: Only when overtaking a road train
s821: There is a risk of a motorcycle being pushed sideways at high speed when overtaking a road train, in a strong crosswind, and if the two front brake discs act differently from each other when braking.
